Power Stage 0: Design and procurement
note: Draft dates, from the power lead's completion-stage document. Complete when: the design is frozen and all parts are ordered. Activities: Finalise the single-line diagram and sizing (8.8 kW PV, 8 kW inverter, 20 kWh battery, 10 kW generator); write the HPTS transfer logic; design the mains-generator interlocks; order solar and missing HPTS parts; confirm site readiness in writing.

name: Power Stage 1: HPTS development and generator modification
note: Draft dates, from the power lead's completion-stage document. Complete when: the HPTS hardware and control system work correctly on the bench. Activities: Assemble the HPTS hardware; complete the ESP32 programming with a safe default state; modify the generator control (start, stop, run and fault feedback); integrate switching; test components; bench-test the full sequence with simulated failures.

name: Power Stage 3: Remote monitoring and control
note: Draft dates, from the power lead's completion-stage document. Complete when: the HPTS can be monitored and controlled remotely and keeps working if the connection drops. Activities: Internet connectivity; web monitoring interface; ESP32 to web platform; remote monitoring; remote control with refused commands; alerts; test that the HPTS keeps switching locally when the internet is lost. Depends on the web and embedded teams.

name: Power Stage 2: Testing and validation of the HPTS
note: Draft dates, from the power lead's completion-stage document. Complete when: the HPTS has passed every test on all currently available sources. Activities: Test on available sources; test automatic switching and power interruptions; test fault cases (generator fails to start, flickering mains, manual override); test protection; write the test report.

name: Power Stage 4: Solar system installation
note: Draft dates, from the power lead's completion-stage document. Complete when: the solar system is installed, tested and can supply electricity on its own. Activities: Check delivered components; prepare the site; install panels and mounting, inverter and battery; wire and protect; inspect before energising; test and commission. Needs the building and roof ready.

name: Power Stage 5: Integration of the HPTS with the power sources
note: Draft dates, from the power lead's completion-stage document. Complete when: all three sources are connected to the HPTS and protection is verified. Activities: Finalise the connection arrangement; connect the HPTS to solar, mains and generator; integrate source selection (solar, mains, generator, with battery thresholds); verify protection, isolation and the interlock.

name: Power Stage 6: Full system integration and testing
note: Draft dates, from the power lead's completion-stage document. Complete when: the complete power system runs reliably under normal and changing conditions. Activities: Test on solar, mains and generator; test transitions and the full outage sequence including battery low; test remote control under real conditions; extended operational testing over an agreed trial period; resolve issues. The trial period is still to be agreed.

name: Power Stage 7: Final commissioning and documentation
note: Draft dates, from the power lead's completion-stage document. Complete when: the system is documented, accepted and handed over. Activities: Final inspection; technical documentation and circuit diagrams; operating instructions and operator training; commissioning report; handover.

name: Embedded Stage 0: Architecture freeze and collaboration setup
note: Draft dates. Complete when: the architecture and interfaces are frozen, the Rajtronics agreement is signed, and the team and workspace are in place. Activities: 0.1 Freeze the embedded architecture: HGC, SOM, RS-485 bus and the HPTS interface. 0.2 Decide the open design choices: current-sensing method, relay now or solid-state later, protection layers, current rating per outlet, and how the HGC links to the HPTS. 0.3 Agree interface specifications with the power lead (HPTS inputs, outputs, status, generator start, stop and run feedback) and the web lead (MQTT topics, device identity, OTA, device shadow). 0.4 Sign the collaboration agreement with Rajtronics: confidentiality, ownership of results, six-month initial term. 0.5 Agree the Rajtronics workspace, access hours, equipment and named contacts; set a monthly review meeting. 0.6 Select the 3 to 5 pilot team members jointly with Rajtronics, from interns and short-term contract staff, and set tasks and supervision.

name: Embedded Stage 1: Hardware sourcing and manufacturer selection
note: Draft dates. Complete when: a manufacturer is selected and ready for the pilot order once funding is secured. Activities: 1.1 Finalise the RFQ package with the HPTS and embedded details and a bill of materials. 1.2 Send the RFQ to shortlisted manufacturers and answer their questions. 1.3 Compare quotes on price, lead time, quality and willingness to hand over editable design files. 1.4 Select the manufacturer and agree terms on design ownership and file handover. 1.5 Make first contact with NEMSA, NCC and SON on electrical, radio-bearing and imported parts.

name: Embedded Stage 2: Smart outlet module (SOM) design and firmware
note: Draft dates. Complete when: a single SOM works on the bench and protects itself on its own. Activities: 2.1 Design the SOM circuit: relay, metering, temperature sensing, local protection and isolated RS-485 interface. 2.2 Write the SOM firmware: switching, measurement, session limits, fault flags and Modbus-RTU registers. 2.3 Implement local protection that trips on over-current, voltage fault, over-temperature and stuck relay. 2.4 Define and test behaviour on bus loss: keep running sessions safe and enforce its own limits. 2.5 Calibrate and test metering accuracy against a reference meter.

name: Embedded Stage 3: Hub gateway controller (HGC) design and firmware
note: Draft dates. Complete when: the HGC runs a full set of SOMs on the bench, with and without internet. Activities: 3.1 Design the HGC: ESP32-S3 class processor, isolated RS-485 master, flash storage, battery-backed clock, keypad, display, QR reader and secure element. 3.2 Write core firmware: poll up to 50 SOMs in turn over Modbus-RTU, send commands and record events. 3.3 Implement passcode validation against an authorised-user list stored on the HGC. 3.4 Implement safe over-the-air update with a spare slot and fall-back to the old version. 3.5 Implement the offline event log and upload when the connection returns. 3.6 Make the HGC fail safe: never override an outlet trip, and settle to a safe state if it resets or hangs.

name: Embedded Stage 4: PCB design and prototype boards
note: Draft dates. Complete when: the boards pass their individual tests and the design is frozen with all files handed over. Activities: 4.1 Agree the board split (HPTS controller led by power, SOM, HGC), the design tool and who draws each board. 4.2 Draw the SOM and HGC boards with RS-485 protection and termination, surge protection at every connector, isolation, test points and a programming header. 4.3 Fabricate and assemble the first prototype boards. 4.4 Test each board alone under supervision, with proper isolation and protection. 4.5 Freeze the design and hand over editable design files, manufacturing outputs, a bill of materials with exact part numbers and bring-up notes.

name: Design frozen and pilot batch order placed
note: Needs the funds milestone (15 Jan 2027) and the Stage 4.5 design freeze.

name: Embedded Stage 5: Bench integration with the HPTS and the cloud
note: Draft dates. Complete when: the HGC exchanges status and commands with both the HPTS and the cloud, and keeps working offline. Activities: 5.1 Join SOMs, HGC and HPTS on a bench with real loads; measure accuracy and timing. 5.2 Implement the HGC to HPTS interface agreed in Stage 0. 5.3 Test that source-change and fault alerts from the HPTS reach the HGC. 5.4 Connect the HGC to AWS IoT Core over MQTT/TLS using its device identity. 5.5 Implement device shadow, commands, telemetry and OTA delivery with the web lead. 5.6 Test with the internet cut: switching and charging continue locally.

name: Embedded Stage 6: Pilot batch, manufacture, shipping and delivery
note: Draft dates. Complete when: the pilot hardware is in Ibadan, checked and ready to install. The date assumes about 16 weeks from order to delivery. Activities: 6.1 Place the pilot batch order once the design is frozen and funds are secured. 6.2 Supervise manufacture and run acceptance tests on the first units. 6.3 Arrange shipping, customs and delivery to Ibadan. 6.4 Count and check the delivered hardware and spares.

name: Hardware delivered in Ibadan
Embedded Stage 7: Station integration, field testing and handover
note: Draft dates. Complete when: the embedded system runs reliably in the station and is documented and handed over. Activities: 7.1 Install the HGC and SOMs at the station with the site and power teams. 7.2 Run end-to-end tests with the web platform: booking, passcode, socket unlock, metering and billing record. 7.3 Test fault cases: bus loss, outlet trip, power outage and stuck relay. 7.4 Run an extended operation test over the agreed trial period. 7.5 Prepare technical documentation, test results and a maintenance guide; train the station attendants. 7.6 Review the Rajtronics collaboration at the end of the initial six-month term and agree next steps.

name: Web Stage 0: Prototype review and delivery planning
note: Draft dates, from the web lead's completion-stage document. Complete when: the baseline, scope and workstreams are agreed. Activities: Review the PHP prototype; map reuse versus new build; confirm user groups and surfaces; break the architecture into workstreams and dependencies.

name: Web Stage 1: Design system and UX development
note: Draft dates, from the web lead's completion-stage document. Complete when: the design system, key screens, booking click-demo and component specs are ready for frontend work. Activities: Evolve the brand design system; review prototype UX screens; build the Figma click-demo for the booking journey; build the component library and design-token specification.

name: Web Stage 3: API gateway and authentication
note: Draft dates, from the web lead's completion-stage document. Complete when: frontend apps and devices can communicate through the API and authentication layer. Activities: REST and WebSocket API gateway; Cognito and JWT authentication; role-based access and MFA; device mutual TLS.

name: Web Stage 5: Data stores, integrations and device-cloud edge
note: Draft dates, from the web lead's completion-stage document. Complete when: the data layer, integrations and device-cloud communication are connected. Activities: Aurora/Postgres; DynamoDB and Timestream; S3 and CDN; Paystack or Flutterwave, Termii or Twilio SMS, SES email, FCM and APNs push; connect hub gateway controllers to AWS IoT Core over MQTT/TLS; device shadows and commands. Device connection depends on embedded Stage 5.

name: Web Stage 4: Backend services development
note: Draft dates, from the web lead's completion-stage document. Complete when: core and supporting backend services are available with the prototype logic kept where specified. Activities: User and station services; reuse and evolve booking logic, PIN/token logic and the earliest-free-socket availability engine; payment and energy services; device OTA and shadow, notifications and analytics services.

name: Web Stage 2: Frontend application development
note: Draft dates, from the web lead's completion-stage document. Complete when: the customer web, admin and mobile PWA are implemented and ready to connect to services. Activities: Customer web app (React / Next.js); admin and operator console; mobile PWA first with React Native later; maps and live status with Mapbox and WebSocket.

name: Web Stage 6: Integration, testing and release readiness
note: Draft dates, from the web lead's completion-stage document. Complete when: the integrated platform has passed its functional and integration checks and is ready for release planning. Activities: Integrate frontend, API and backend; verify authentication, roles, MFA and device mTLS; test booking, PIN and availability; test payments, notifications and maps; test device communication over MQTT/TLS; test all three apps; resolve issues.
